prompts.title: Product page with a claims check
prompts.summary: Writes a product page from texture, scent and ingredients, then flags any line that sounds like a medical claim.
prompts.prompt:
Write the product page for [product] from [brand]. Facts: texture [ ], scent [ ], key ingredients [ ], size [ ], how to use it [ ], price [ ].

Rules: describe how it feels, smells and is used. Never say it treats, cures, heals, prevents or repairs anything, and never name a skin condition (like acne, eczema or rosacea). Never say SPF or sun protection, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, collagen-boosting or detox. Don't use clinically proven, dermatologist tested or recommended, hypoallergenic, non-comedogenic, non-toxic, clean, natural or organic unless I write "proof on file" next to it. Never "chemical-free". After the page, list any sentence you're unsure about and why.
prompts.use: Run it on every new product, and on old pages once. Ask a lawyer about anything the check flags.

prompts.title: Routine guide
prompts.summary: Builds a morning and night routine from the products you sell, in the order to use them.
prompts.prompt: Here are the products [brand] sells: [list with what each is]. Build a simple morning routine and a night routine from them, in order, with one line on how much to use and how. Add a short version for someone who owns one product. No promises about results.
prompts.use: Use it as a page, a carousel and the second welcome email.

prompts.title: Creator brief
prompts.summary: A UGC brief for one product: the shots, what to say and the words to stay away from.
prompts.prompt: Write a UGC brief for [product] from [brand]. Include: who the creator is talking to, the first two seconds, five shots, three things they can say in their own words (texture, scent, how they use it), the words they must not use (cures, fixes, treats, any skin condition by name, SPF or sun protection, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, collagen-boosting, detox, chemical-free), that they use the product before filming and say only what they found, no before-and-after, the #ad line, and the usage rights we're asking for: [where and how long].
prompts.use: Send it with the product. Keep the do-not-say list in every brief.

notes: This pack writes the words. It doesn't make a product or label legal. FDA's cosmetics law (MoCRA) applies to small brands too: a US contact on the label for reporting problems, safety records, and reporting serious reactions.

Never say SPF or sun protection, name a condition (like acne, eczema or rosacea), or say antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, collagen-boosting or detox. Keep proof on file before you say clinically proven, dermatologist tested or recommended, hypoallergenic, non-comedogenic, non-toxic, clean, natural or organic. Never "chemical-free".
Creators use the product before filming and say only what they found. No before-and-after.
